title: Hybrid Pairs Trading: Cointegration + Ensemble Learning
summary: Integrates cointegration-based pair selection with ensemble ML (likely gradient boosting / stacking) for entry/exit signal generation. Claims to 'substantially outperform traditional statistical approaches to pairs trading' via better signal precision on both entry and exit. ACM conference paper, published approximately May 2026.
why_relevant: H200 (graphical matching pairs) was NOT CONFIRMED — 0/15 pairs cointegrated in US large-cap. H169 (LLM pair selection) is BLOCKED — no open-source implementation found in recent literature. This paper directly addresses the H169/H200 gap: it's not LLM-based but rather ensemble ML for signal quality improvement. Key question: does it address pair SELECTION quality (finding cointegrated pairs) or SIGNAL quality (improving entry/exit once pairs are found)? From snippet, it appears to focus on entry/exit signals — the pair selection problem (H200's root cause failure) may still not be solved.
proposed_action: 1. Update wiki/trading/algorithms/pairs-trading.md: note this paper under 'Recent developments' as a signal-quality enhancement. 2. Add note that the pair SELECTION problem for US large-cap is still the binding constraint (H200 result); ensemble ML on entry/exit doesn't help if no cointegrated pairs found.
caveat: Limited info from snippet alone. The DOI pattern 10.1145/3800000.x suggests ACM SIGKDD or similar. Need full paper to confirm whether this addresses selection or signal quality. Stage as low-risk wiki note rather than new hypothesis.
novelty: MEDIUM — ensemble + cointegration is a known pairing but recent paper with claimed strong results
